The name is a part of the Islamic concept of "taharat", which refers to spiritual and moral purity. The name is associated with the qualities of purity and cleanliness, and is considered a noble and virtuous name in Islamic tradition. The name is also associated with the Quranic concept of "taharat", which refers to the state of being free from impurities and moral defilement. The name is considered a symbol of spiritual growth and development, and is often given to children born into Muslim families. The name has a rich history and cultural significance in Islamic tradition, and is considered a beautiful and meaningful name in many Muslim cultures.
